builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Systematic Comparison of Search Space Complexity and Efficiency for Time-Synchronous End-to-End ASR Models
summary: The method replaces fixed small beam search without an external LM in CTC and neural-transducer decoding with score-based pruning whose effective beam width adapts to model uncertainty. It costs more complex decoder logic and variable per-frame hypothesis counts, including temporary search-space peaks during uncertain audio segments. It can fail when peak hypothesis counts violate worst-case latency budgets in streaming deployments, and the findings transfer poorly to encoder-decoder attention models, which the study does not cover.
rationale: The technique is directly implementable in existing CTC/transducer decoding pipelines without extra hardware, but its benefit depends on the reader's specific ASR workload and latency constraints, so workload-specific validation is warranted.
technique: Score-based adaptive pruning for E2E ASR beam search

claims.statement: The method replaces fixed small beam search without an external LM in CTC and neural-transducer decoding with score-based pruning whose effective beam width adapts to model uncertainty. It costs more complex decoder logic and variable per-frame hypothesis counts, including temporary search-space peaks during uncertain audio segments. It can fail when peak hypothesis counts violate worst-case latency budgets in streaming deployments, and the findings transfer poorly to encoder-decoder attention models, which the study does not cover.

Score-based pruning dynamically adapts the search to model uncertainty, leading to a significantly lower Real-Time Factor (RTF) than low fixed-size beam pruning; the abstract reports no numeric factor.
